# F2 · Correcting the squad from two screenshots

*Extracted verbatim from the PRD, which remains the single source of truth for every criterion below. Edit the PRD, then regenerate — never edit this file.*

Identifiers in this file: `F2-AC-01` – `F2-UP-03`.

#### F2 · Correcting the squad from two screenshots

| Section | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Priority | **Must.** 2.5 calls the screenshot correction a hard requirement — without it, calls get built on stale squad state whenever Stephen has made an unlogged change. |
| Serves | The first core job in Section 2.3: FPL's public feed only exposes the squad as at the last deadline, so a change made since then is invisible to the app and would poison every call built on it. |
| Happy path | The manager taps *Update*, reads what will be taken from each picture, supplies two screenshots — FPL's Team (squad/pitch) screen and its Transfers screen, each chosen from the camera roll — and the app replaces the stored squad with what it read from both. No single FPL screen carries everything the parse needs, so two are required — clunkier, but it's what the FPL app offers. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **F2-AC-01** | The sheet states, before any picture is chosen, what will be read from the **Team** screenshot: starting eleven, bench order, captain and vice-captain, and chips remaining. |
| **F2-AC-02** | The sheet states, before any picture is chosen, what will be read from the **Transfers** screenshot: bank and free transfers. |
| **F2-AC-03** | Each of the two screenshots is chosen from the camera roll. There is no in-app camera capture — the source is always an existing screenshot, never a live photo. |
| **F2-AC-04** | A successful read of both replaces the squad wholesale: the two screenshots are the source of truth for that week, not a diff applied to the last-deadline squad. |
| **F2-AC-05** | After a successful read the app returns through the Thinking state with the corrected squad. |
| **F2-AC-06** | **The correction runs through F6's regeneration, not a separate path.** Selected calls survive and rejected calls stay suppressed exactly as in any refresh. |
| **F2-AC-07** | **The one exception only a squad correction can produce:** where the new squad contradicts a selected call — the screenshot shows something other than what that call expected — the screenshot wins, the lock is broken and dropped, and the manager is told why through the same refresh diff, rather than the app keeping a stale lock or silently discarding it. |
| **F2-AC-08** | The Squad screen carries no indicator of where the current squad data came from. The manager already knows whether he has just uploaded, so the screen does not need to state it; **the Assistant states it instead, on its editorial card (F8).** |
| **Unhappy Paths** |  |
| **F2-UP-01** | **Only part of the squad reads cleanly, from either screenshot.** Acceptance: the update is all-or-nothing across both images. Anything short of all fifteen players plus the chip row from the Team screenshot, and both bank and free transfers from the Transfers screenshot, is a failure: nothing is applied, the existing squad is untouched, and an *Upload failed* screen states that the squad was not updated, gives the reason and names which screenshot it came from (e.g. "only 4 of 15 players legible on the Team screenshot", "free transfers not found on the Transfers screenshot"), lists the three common causes — a cropped screenshot, a photo of a screen rather than a screenshot, the wrong screen entirely — and offers the same upload actions again for whichever screenshot failed. There is no confirm-and-correct screen and no manual gap filling. |
| **F2-UP-02** | **Either screenshot is of someone else's team, or last week's.** Acceptance: an accepted risk, not gated. The app has no way to know whose squad a clean picture shows; the cost of being wrong is that the local squad is replaced (never the FPL account), and the next upload or the gameweek rollover corrects it. |
| **F2-UP-03** | **Photo library access is denied.** Acceptance: no bespoke denied state is built; the operating system's own prompt is the route back. Parked (3.4, deferred items) — revisited only if the app is ever shared. |
